items.canonicalSource: 20.01.03-fan-preference-centre.md:42-63 ("### Frequency Tiers (see D-05)" — "Frequency is a **per-(fan, entity)** setting"; Highlights = "At most **1 marketing email per calendar month** from this entity", "The 2nd+ marketing send in a month is **dropped, not queued**"; "**Send-time resolution** (this feature writes the state; [20.03] reads it)" … "**and** the tier's frequency cap is not already exhausted for the period") and 20.01.03-fan-preference-centre.md:163 (D-05).
items.summary: The finding is right that 20.02 owns no frequency policy — a grep of the whole domain returns per-fan frequency capping only in 20.03.03 and in 20.01.03. But the auditor's inference that no owner exists anywhere is wrong: 20.01.03 D-05 owns exactly the object DT-04 describes — a per-(fan, entity), per-artist marketing budget the artist cannot widen, written by the Preference Centre and read by 20.03 at send-time. DT-04 rules out *throttling* as the same object; it never rules out the 20.01.03 tiers, which it does not mention. So 20.03.03's three restatements had drifted onto a file that holds nothing, and the '`-cx.md` frequency-fatigue thread' they cite does not exist. Fixed all four: the overlapping-campaigns edge case now resolves against 20.01.03 D-05 with its real period (calendar month, not 'today') and its real disposition ('dropped, not queued', not 'deferred or suppressed'), and the UI copy follows; DT-04's 'lives with segmentation/fan-fatigue' now names 20.01.03 D-05 and quotes its writes-here/reads-there rule; the Cross-Cut Note points at 20.01.03 and at 20.01-…-cx.md CX-03 (the real thread — the Preference Centre is the only writer of that state) instead of the non-existent one; D-08 keeps its substance and names the owner. One genuine sub-question survived and would otherwise have been invented, so it is tracked rather than answered: 20.01.03's default tier is **All**, i.e. uncapped, so a fan who never opens the Preference Centre has no cap at all — whether a platform-imposed floor should exist on top of the fan-authored tiers, over what period and at what value, is nowhere in the tree. Logged as 20.03.03 Q-04, [OWNER], User, deferred to /create-prd.
items.ownerBrief: Tracked in-file as 20.03.03 Q-04 (User, /create-prd): the per-fan frequency cap now correctly resolves to the fan's own tier (20.01.03 D-05), whose default is 'All' = uncapped. That means nothing stops an artist sending twice in an hour to a fan who never touched their preferences. Decide whether the platform imposes a default fatigue budget above the fan-authored tiers — and if so its period and value. A floor protects fans and the shared sending reputation; no floor keeps an artist's reach over a list they own unrestricted. This is not blocking any downstream stage, since the specified behaviour (fan tiers) is now complete and buildable on its own.

items.summary: The contradiction holds. 20.01.01's Partial-data row asserted a record-level marketing gate keyed on identity-key strength, which by the file's own key ranking captures every import-only record and so hard-disables the exact records 20.01.04's happy path and D-03 send warm-up mail to. The drifted side is 20.01.01: it is not the owner of contactability — line 32 of the same file says so ('governed entirely by 20.01.02') — and neither 20.01.02 nor the sub-domain CX map records any identity-verification input to contactability; 20.01.02 D-02 resolves it off the consent ledger alone, and the only 20.01.01→consent constraint recorded anywhere is CX-02's merge intersection. The owning side is a numbered decision (20.01.04 D-03) in the file that owns import. Rewrote the row: key strength gates resolution/auto-merge (D-02) and nothing else; marketability defers to 20.01.02 D-02/D-07 and, for imports, to 20.01.04 D-03's tiering. Kept what 20.01.01 legitimately owns — a record whose only key is a payment fingerprint or a processor-hidden email has no marketing-capable address, so it is not contactable as a matter of fact, which preserves the two guest-purchase rows above it. Deliberately did NOT settle the consent-provenance axis (whether artist-asserted-only records are sendable-with-warning or blocked until re-permissioned): that is genuinely open and already tracked, so the row now cites it — 20.01-…-cx.md CX-01 q3 and 20.01.04 Q-01 (User, /create-prd-security).

Tier, join date and active-vs-lapsed are 20.05.01's state; 20.04 has no membership concept at all, and the dependency already runs the other way (20.05.01 feeds 20.02.02). The adjacent rows in the same table cite their sources precisely ('19 Ticketing', 'CX-M13', '20.02.02, 20.03'), so a loose parent-level shorthand is not the convention here. Changed the Membership row's Source domain from 20.04 to 20.05.01 (3-column table preserved) and added the missing Cross-Cut Note — the finding's second half, that 20.02.01's Cross-Cut Notes never referenced 20.05 at all, was also true, so the read dependency was invisible from this node.
